name: Sweet Rusk
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Make a sponge with the milk, yeast, and enough flour for a thin batter
In the morning add the butter, eggs, and sugar, previously beaten up well together, the salt, and flour enough to make a soft dough
Mould with the hands into balls of uniform size
Set close together in a pan
Let them rise until very light
After baking, wash the tops with a clean soft cloth dipped in molasses and water

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Make a sponge with the milk, yeast, and enough flour for a thin batter
2. Let it rise over night
3. In the morning add the butter, eggs, and sugar, previously beaten up well together, the salt, and flour enough to make a soft dough
4. Mould with the hands into balls of uniform size
5. Set close together in a pan
6. Let them rise until very light
7. After baking, wash the tops with a clean soft cloth dipped in molasses and water
